title: Israeli company Redefine Meat prints a plant-based steak in three dimensions that is served in restaurants and sold in shops in Europe

trailer.text: Redefine Meat is an Israeli startup that produces meat substitutes without animal ingredients, using three-dimensional printing.
The company was founded by Eshchar Ben-Shitrit and Adam Lahav.
The company's printers take three plant-based blends, Alt-Muscle, Alt-Fat and Alt-Blood, and combine them into a multi-layered plant-based steak.
According to BGR, restaurants in London, Berlin and Amsterdam serve the printed steaks, among them restaurants of chef Marco Pierre White.
Since July 2024 the company's flagship steak has been sold in the UK through Ocado and in Switzerland through Coop.

stations.title: The challenge: a real cut of meat

paragraphs.text: Plant-based ground meat substitutes have been on the market for several years.
Mimicking a real cut of meat has proved a much greater challenge.
A plant-based steak that looks real is considered the holy grail of the alternative meat industry.
According to the CEO, the beef category has a large variety of products that meat substitutes do not provide.
According to Food Dive, other companies that do not use three-dimensional printing had already worked on steak substitutes, and Beyond Meat and Impossible Foods said they were working on steaks.
According to the UN Food and Agriculture Organization, in 2018 alone about 302 million cattle, 69 billion chickens and 1.5 billion pigs were slaughtered for meat.
According to the FAO's estimate, the world's livestock is responsible for 14.5% of all human-caused greenhouse gas emissions.
According to EIT Food, Eshchar Ben-Shitrit previously practised law at the Supreme Court of Israel and later moved into the world of technology.
After becoming a father, he did something he once thought impossible: he stopped eating meat.
According to Food Dive, on the day his second son was born he left his job as a product manager in the world of three-dimensional printing.
Ben-Shitrit said that he lives in a small village near Jerusalem and that he became determined to find a way to enjoy meat without harming animals.
He is vegetarian, and so he was disqualified from being a formal taster at his own company.
He founded Redefine Meat with his partner Adam Lahav.
According to Ben-Shitrit, a meatless steak that resembles the muscle of an animal requires a special three-dimensional printer.
He said that no one had such a printer until then, and that the company developed it over the preceding two years.

stations.title: The printer: plant-based muscle, fat and blood

paragraphs.text: The company used an industrial three-dimensional printer of its own and several materials to print the steak, layer by layer.
The printers take three plant-based blends, Alt-Muscle, Alt-Fat and Alt-Blood, and combine them into a single steak.
According to Food Dive, the printer can print in dots smaller than a millimetre.
A patent application was filed for the technology.
The steak is made from soy and pea proteins, coconut fat and sunflower oil, with natural colours and flavours.
Ben-Shitrit said that the company did not create any new ingredients, mainly so that there would be no obstacles on the way to market.
Together with flavour expert Givaudan, butchers, chefs and food technologists, the company digitally mapped more than 70 sensory parameters.
Ben-Shitrit said that the printer produced a single piece weighing about five pounds.
According to 3DPrint.com, in 2020 the company reached a printing speed of 10 kilograms per hour.
The company unveiled the "Alt-Steak", which it says reproduces the texture, taste and appearance of real meat.
Founder and CEO Ben-Shitrit says that it looks, cooks and tastes like the original.
According to him, the idea had so far been welcomed by the butchers the company works with.
In Tel Aviv the company held a blind tasting among meat-eaters.
Ben-Shitrit said that more than 90% of the more than 600 tasters were genuinely astonished to discover that the meat did not come from an animal.
According to Food Dive, the company announced that the Alt-Steak would be tested at high-end restaurants in Israel, Germany and Switzerland.
In 2020 Ben-Shitrit said that the steak would reach restaurants in Israel that year and supermarkets in 2022.
According to him, the price would initially be about the same as that of a regular meat steak.
In January 2021 the company signed a first deal with the Israeli meat distributor Best Meister.
According to Globes, the company received approval to market in Israel and Singapore, and in the first stage the products will be sold to restaurants.
Redefine Meat completed a $29 million Series A funding round, led by Happiness Capital and Hanaco Ventures.
According to Globes, this is the largest Series A round ever by a meat alternatives company.
According to Globes, the money will make it possible to launch products in Europe, Asia and North America and to set up a production plant in Israel.
According to FoodNavigator, the company said that the funding brings it closer to its goal of becoming the world's largest alternative meat company by 2030.
According to 3DPrint.com, the company later raised another $135 million, in a round completed on 23 August 2021.
Ben-Shitrit explained that the business model is selling the company's industrial printers to meat distributors.
According to him, the company wants to change the belief that tasty meat can only come from animals.

stations.title: On the plate: restaurants and stores

paragraphs.text: According to BGR, the printed meat mimics flank steak, also known as bavette.
According to Tech Brew, the Israeli startup reached more than 30 restaurants in London, Berlin and Amsterdam.

According to BGR, chef Marco Pierre White's restaurants and three other restaurants in the London area will serve Redefine Meat products for £20 to £30, a price similar to what they charge for a regular beef steak.
According to 3DPrint.com, the products are served in 86 restaurants, hotels and bars in Israel.
Since July 2024 the flagship steak can be bought in the UK at Ocado and in Switzerland at Coop.
According to FoodNavigator, this is the first time the flank steak has been sold directly to consumers in Europe.
In 2024 Ben-Shitrit said that the company had introduced the world's first printed steak and that it sells it in five countries.
He said that the steak costs about the same as an animal steak.
Ben-Shitrit said that the product portfolio will include more cuts such as entrecôte, fillet, sirloin and brisket.

At that time, when the company was focused only on developing the Alt-Steak and expanding it in restaurants, Ben-Shitrit said the company would not work on any kind of meat other than beef in the near future.
According to 3DPrint.com, the company received excellent reviews from leading chefs and Michelin chefs, among them Marco Pierre White.
According to EIT Food, Redefine Meat won the first year of the organisation's RFS programme.

According to the company's estimate, a person who eats a hamburger twice a week all their life and switches to its products will save 43.5 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent and 14,600 litres of water.
The company's description claims that its meat is 95% more sustainable, healthier and cheaper than beef.
According to 3DPrint.com, the company grew to 140 employees, including a new team in Europe.
According to a partner at Hanaco Ventures, the company grew to more than 40 employees during 2020, despite the coronavirus.
According to FoodNavigator, in Europe there is growing opposition to meat substitutes that are regarded as ultra-processed food, and this makes it harder to get shoppers to come back.

In an EIT Food Consumer Observatory survey of nearly 10,000 people in 17 European countries, 54% said that concern about ultra-processed food deters them from buying products such as plant-based burgers and sausages.
Ben-Shitrit admitted that the company is a technology company, and said that its processes are transparent.

claims.text: לפי Tech Brew, הסטארט-אפ הישראלי הרחיב לאירופה עם יותר מ-30 מסעדות בלונדון, ברלין ואמסטרדם.
claims.quote: Israeli startup Redefine Meat, which 3D-prints plant-based steaks, expanded into Europe, with 30+ restaurants in London, Berlin, and Amsterdam.

claims.text: לפי BGR, שלוש מסעדות נוספות באזור לונדון יגישו את מוצרי רדיפיין מיט במחיר של 20 עד 30 לירות שטרלינג.
claims.quote: three other restaurants in the London area will serve Redefine Meat for £20 to £30.

claims.text: לפי 3DPrint.com, מוצרי החברה מוגשים ב-86 מסעדות, מלונות ובארים בישראל.
claims.quote: Today, New-Meat products thrive in 86 Israeli restaurants, hotels, and bars

claims.text: לפי FoodNavigator, מוצרי החברה זמינים בשירותי מזון בתשע מדינות, וזו הפעם הראשונה שסטייק הפלנק נמכר ישירות לצרכנים באירופה.
claims.quote: Already available via foodservice across nine countries, the launches mark the first time that the flank steak has been made available direct to European consumers.

claims.text: בן-שטרית אמר ב-2024 שהחברה הציגה את הסטייק המודפס הראשון בעולם ושהיא מוכרת אותו כעת בחמש מדינות.
claims.quote: We even introduced the world’s first 3D-printed steak, which we now sell in five countries.

claims.text: בן-שטרית אמר ב-2024 שסטייק הצמח של החברה עולה כיום בערך כמו סטייק מן החי.
claims.quote: Right now, our plant-based steak costs about the same as an animal steak

claims.text: בן-שטרית אמר שתיק המוצרים יכלול נתחי בקר שונים כמו אנטרקוט, פילה, סירלוין וחזה.
claims.quote: Our portfolio will include different whole cuts of beef, such as entrecôte, fillet, sirloin, and brisket.

claims.text: בן-שטרית אמר שהחברה לא תעבוד בעתיד הקרוב על סוג בשר אחר מלבד בקר.
claims.quote: Ben-Shitrit said the company is not going to be working on any other kind of meat in the near future.

claims.text: לפי 3DPrint.com, החברה קיבלה ביקורות מצוינות משפים יוקרתיים ושפי מישלן, בהם מרקו פיירו ווייט.
claims.quote: Redefine Meat has gotten top reviews from high-end and Michelin-star chefs, including legendary British chef Marco Pierre White

claims.text: לפי הערכת החברה, אדם שאוכל המבורגר פעמיים בשבוע לאורך חייו יחסוך במעבר למוצריה 43.5 טונות שווה ערך פחמן דו-חמצני ו-14,600 ליטר מים.
claims.quote: Redefine Meat estimates the carbon savings of moving to its meat as 43.5 tonnes of carbon dioxide-equivalent (CO2e) and water savings of 14,600 litres.

claims.text: בתיאור החברה נטען שהבשר החלופי שלה בר-קיימא ב-95% יותר, בריא משמעותית יותר וזול מבקר.
claims.quote: alt-meat is 95% more sustainable, significantly healthier and costs less than beef.

claims.text: לפי 3DPrint.com, החברה גדלה מעשרה עובדים ב-2019 ל-140 בשנת הכתבה, כולל צוות חדש באירופה.
claims.quote: the company went from only ten employees in 2019 to 140 this year, including a new team in Europe.

claims.text: לדברי שותף ב-Hanaco Ventures, החברה גדלה מ-8 עובדים ליותר מ-40 במהלך 2020 למרות אתגרי הקורונה.
claims.quote: have watched the company rapidly grow from eight people to more than 40, despite the challenges of Covid-19

claims.text: לפי FoodNavigator, התנגדות גוברת באירופה לתחליפי בשר שמוגדרים כמזון אולטרה-מעובד מקשה על השגת רכישות חוזרות במגזר.
claims.quote: Achieving that higher repeat purchase rate has been made more challenging for the sector by a growing pushback in Europe against meat alternatives that they class as ultra-processed foods (UPFs).

claims.text: לפי סקר של EIT Food Consumer Observatory בקרב כמעט 10,000 איש ב-17 מדינות באירופה, 54% אומרים שהם נרתעים מקניית מוצרים כמו המבורגרים ונקניקיות צמחיים בגלל החשש שהם מזון אולטרה-מעובד.
claims.quote: which surveyed nearly 10,000 people across 17 European countries, 54% say they’re deterred from adding products like plant-based burgers, sausages and mince to supermarket trollies

claims.text: בן-שטרית הודה שהחברה היא חברת טכנולוגיה, ואמר שהתהליכים שלה שקופים.
claims.quote: We have to be honest, we are a technology company

claims.text: לפי 3DPrint.com, סך הגיוסים של החברה עד אז עלה על 170 מיליון דולר.
claims.quote: bringing its total funding to date to over $170 million.

claims.text: לפי כתבה אחת, בן-שטרית ייסד את החברה בנס ציונה.
claims.quote: Founded by Ben-Sheetrit in Ness Ziona, the company creates a variety of new meat products

claims.text: בראיון ב-2024 אמר בן-שטרית שהפסיק לאכול בשר לפני כעשר שנים.
claims.quote: a father of three, and I stopped eating meat about 10 years ago

claims.text: לפי EIT Food, פחות משנה אחרי ההשקה המסחרית נמצאים מוצרי החברה כמעט באלף נקודות שירות מזון.
claims.quote: In less than 12 months since commercially launching in the UK, Germany, Netherlands, France, and Israel, today almost 1,000 food service locations are serving New Meat.

claims.text: לפי 3DPrint.com, מוצרי החברה זמינים ביותר מ-120 מסעדות בישראל, הולנד, גרמניה ובריטניה.
claims.quote: New-Meat products can be found in over 120 restaurants in Israel, the Netherlands, Germany, and the UK.

claims.text: בן-שטרית אמר בנובמבר 2024 שמוצרי החברה נמצאים בכ-5,000 מסעדות ברחבי אירופה.
claims.quote: our products in around 5,000 restaurants across Europe

claims.text: ההון החדש נועד לתמוך בהשקה מסחרית ובצמיחה בינלאומית ב-2021, עם השלמת מתקן ייצור גדול למדפסות התלת-ממד התעשייתיות.
claims.quote: support its commercial launch and international growth in 2021, on the back of the slated completion of a large-scale production facility

claims.text: לפי Tech Brew, החברה שואפת להיות ב"אלפי" מסעדות ברחבי אירופה עד סוף השנה הבאה.
claims.quote: Redefine Meat aims to be in “thousands” of restaurants across Europe by the end of next year
